## Lane and scope
Lane `avra-lane-laws-fusion`, working for the Lead (controller) over claude-bridge. It started by
fusing the program layer's laws into one driver (NodeKind `on`, `judge(view, at)`, findings
identical, warm == cold). Since then it has been a series of CPU cuts in the program layer,

/// One variant's tag arm — the same IDENTITY `shallow_case` folds,
/// answered bare instead of mixed into a fingerprint.
fn tag_case(t: MetaType, v: MetaVariant) -> Arms {
    let lit = int_lit(variant_id(t, v))
    if v.fields.is_empty() { return quote { .${v} -> ${lit} } }
    quote { .${v}(${binders(v)}) -> ${lit} }
}

/// One variant's kids arm.
fn kids_case(t: MetaType, v: MetaVariant) -> Arms {
    if v.fields.is_empty() { return quote { .${v} -> [] } }
    let singles = [single_at(f) for f in v.fields if reached(f) && reach_shape(t, v, f) != null]
    let ats = [c! for c in singles if c != null]
    if !singles.is_empty() && ats.length == singles.length { return quote { .${v}(${binders(v)}) -> [${..ats}] } }
    quote { .${v}(${binders(v)}) -> ${concatenated(reach_parts(t, v))} }
}

/// One variant's kids pushed onto `onto` in `kids_case`'s order, answering how long `onto` then is:
/// an id payload pushed where it lies, any other payload through its kids.
fn pushed_case(t: MetaType, v: MetaVariant) -> Arms {
    if v.fields.is_empty() { return quote { .${v} -> onto.length } }
    let pushes = [pushed_part(f, r!) for f in v.fields if reached(f) for r in [reach_shape(t, v, f)] if r != null]
    if pushes.is_empty() { return quote { .${v}(${binders(v)}) -> onto.length } }
    quote {
        .${v}(${binders(v)}) -> {
            ${..pushes}
            onto.length
        }
    }
}

  2. NO TOOL PATH ADDS TO THE BASELINE. `--accept` only PRUNES what

// Value equality; null equals only null.
// TEXT IS A LENGTH AND BYTES, NEVER A TERMINATOR. A NUL is a
// character like any other — `from_codepoint(0)` mints one with no
// foreign input at all — so a comparison that stops at the first one

- Nothing in the language pushes a batch onto a list in place, and `concat` copies. The idiomatic rewrite would therefore allocate again and undo the walk's point.
- Keeping it would have meant six licensed loops, or adding a new List method that the compiler's own source uses, which has to land in two stages.

The tree after the revert is the version I already measured: findings identical to base55's, cli at 77–78 s.

**2. The string-compare rise: not the kids walk.** With and without it, std-program shows the same count (45,088,840). The rise comes from an earlier lane commit, 629e7cb3, which turned 17 per-item fact queries into lookups on the item's view. Each lookup checks the file's package and path strings in `ItemView.holds`, which went from 1.23M to 1.88M compares on std-program (+0.22%; cli +0.18%).

The planned Name migration doesn't fix this, because creating a Name on each lookup costs the same compare. The real fix is to hand the view directly to laws that read the whole item. That changes the shape of a law declaration, so it also has to land in two stages.

**Decision needed:** I've asked the Lead to choose:
- (a) accept the +0.2% compares in batch 56, given 10% fewer retains and 13% less CPU, with the proper fix next; or
- (b) hold 629e7cb3 out of batch 56 until that fix lands.

The bundle is `/work/avra-lane-laws-fusion.bundle` (base55..c73d1b04); the census tables are in `/work/avra-lane-laws-fusion.md`.

/// Every word in the written item `at` of `file` that cannot be the name it's written as, node by

fn item_misnamed(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> ItemMisnamed {
    if !item_held(engine, file, at) { return misnamed_made(engine, file, at) }
    let view = item_view(engine, file, at)
    let held? = view.misnamed.get() else {
        let made = misnamed_made(engine, file, at)
        view.misnamed.set(made)
        return made
    }
    held

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Moves whole-item laws that read a view family onto `reads_view`: report only, or --write."""
import re, glob, sys, os
os.chdir('/work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler')
write = '--write' in sys.argv
files = sorted(glob.glob('*.av') + glob.glob('laws/*.av'))
src = {f: open(f).read() for f in files}
SIG = 'engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int'
fn_re = lambda name: re.compile(r'\n((?:export )?fn ' + re.escape(name) + r'\(' + re.escape(SIG) + r'\) -> List<Found> \{)(.*?)\n\}', re.S)

# the families: fns of (engine, file, at) that look the view up and hold their answer on it
fams = {}
for f, t in src.items():
    for m in re.finditer(r'\nfn (\w+)\(' + re.escape(SIG) + r'\) -> (\w+) \{\n    if !item_held\(engine, file, at\) \{ return (\w+)\(engine, file, at\) \}\n    let view = item_view\(engine, file, at\)\n    let held\? = view\.(\w+)\.get\(\) else \{\n        let made = \3\(engine, file, at\)\n        view\.\4\.set\(made\)\n        return made\n    \}\n    held\n\}', t):
        fams[m.group(1)] = (f, m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4), m.group(0))
print(len(fams), 'families:', ' '.join(sorted(fams)))
def view_fn(fam): return (fam[5:] if fam.startswith('item_') else fam) + '_in'

callers = lambda name: sum(len(re.findall(r'(?<![\w.])' + re.escape(name) + r'\b', t)) for t in src.values())
moved, skipped = [], []
for f, t in list(src.items()):
    for m in re.finditer(r'export law (\w+) \{(.*?)\n\}', t, re.S):
        r = re.search(r'\n    reads: (\w+)\n', m.group(2))
        if not r: continue
        name = r.group(1)
        dm = fn_re(name).search(t)
        if not dm: skipped.append((m.group(1), name, 'reads fn not in its file or other shape')); continue
        body = dm.group(2)
        if not (re.search(r'\bread_item\(engine, file, at\)', body) or any(re.search(r'(?<![\w.])' + x + r'\(engine, file, at\)', body) for x in fams)):
            continue
        # the law and its def, plus each `reads: name` across the tree, must be the only mentions
        uses = callers(name)
        lawrefs = sum(len(re.findall(r'\n    reads: ' + re.escape(name) + r'\n', s)) for s in src.values())
        if uses != 1 + lawrefs: skipped.append((m.group(1), name, f'{uses} mentions')); continue
        if re.search(r'(let|for|mut) (engine|file|at)\b|\((engine|file|at)\b[^)]*\) ->|\b(engine|file|at) ->|, (at|file|engine)\) ->', body):
            skipped.append((m.group(1), name, 'rebinds engine/file/at')); continue
        moved.append((f, m.group(1), name))

print(len(moved), 'laws move;', len(skipped), 'skipped')
for s in skipped: print('  skip', s)
if not write: sys.exit(0)

done = set()
for f, law, name in moved:
    t = src[f]
    t = re.sub(r'(export law ' + law + r' \{.*?\n    )reads: ' + name + r'\n', r'\1reads_view: ' + name + '\n', t, count=1, flags=re.S)
    if (f, name) not in done:
        done.add((f, name))
        dm = fn_re(name).search(t)
        body = dm.group(2)
        body = body.replace('\n    if !item_held(engine, file, at) { return [] }', '')
        body = re.sub(r'\bread_item\(engine, file, at\)', 'view.item', body)
        for x in fams: body = re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])' + x + r'\(engine, file, at\)', view_fn(x) + '(view)', body)
        body = re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])(engine|file|at)\b(?!\s*:)', r'view.\1', body)
        head = dm.group(1).replace('(' + SIG + ')', '(view: ItemView)')
        t = t[:dm.start()] + '\n' + head + body + '\n}' + t[dm.end():]
    src[f] = t
# each family split: its view form, and the file's form kept for every other reader
for fam, (f, ty, made, cell, whole) in fams.items():
    v = view_fn(fam)
    if not any(re.search(r'\b' + v + r'\(view\)', s) for s in src.values()): continue
    t = src[f]
    new = (f'\nfn {fam}({SIG}) -> {ty} {{\n    if !item_held(engine, file, at) {{ return {made}(engine, file, at) }}\n    {v}(item_view(engine, file, at))\n}}\n\n'
           f'/// What `{fam}` answers through the item\'s `view`, made the first time it is asked.\n'
           f'fn {v}(view: ItemView) -> {ty} {{\n    let held? = view.{cell}.get() else {{\n        let made = {made}(view.engine, view.file, view.at)\n        view.{cell}.set(made)\n        return made\n    }}\n    held\n}}')
    assert t.count(whole) == 1
    src[f] = t.replace(whole, new)
for f, t in src.items():
    if t != open(f).read():
        if 'ItemView' in t and not re.search(r'^use compiler\.\{[^}]*\bItemView\b', t, re.M) and not re.search(r'\bItemView\b', open(f).read()):
            print('  needs ItemView import:', f)
        open(f, 'w').write(t)
EOF

new='''class Def:
    def __init__(s, start, end, head, body, one): s.s, s.e, s.h, s.b, s.one = start, end, head, body, one
    def start(s): return s.s
    def end(s): return s.e
    def group(s, i): return s.h if i == 1 else s.b
class fn_re:
    """A fn of the law seat's shape named `name`: its head, and its body to its own closing brace,
    whether written on its head's line or below it."""
    def __init__(s, name): s.r = re.compile(r'\\n((?:export )?fn ' + re.escape(name) + r'\\(' + re.escape(SIG) + r'\\) -> List<Found> \\{)')
    def search(s, t):
        m = s.r.search(t)
        if not m: return None
        line_end = t.index('\\n', m.end())
        rest = t[m.end():line_end]
        if rest.count('{') - rest.count('}') == -1:
            return Def(m.start(), line_end, m.group(1), rest[:rest.rindex('}')], True)
        close = t.index('\\n}', m.end())
        return Def(m.start(), close + 2, m.group(1), t[m.end():close], False)
'''

  derives and templates copy. Not localized to the query that stores it.

/// on a declaration wearing no annotation; a mark annotation a declaration of the program's own wears
/// that no collect gathers and nothing else it wears reads; each mark a member a `collect enum`
/// wearing no annotation gathers wears, but the one it gathers by.
fn unread_marks(view: ItemView) -> List<Found> {
    let item = view.item
    let store = item.store
    if !store.refusals().all(lexed_past(it)) { return [] }
    let claimed = compiler_marks()
    let written = [unread_at(m.span, m.name, "", claimed) for s in item.stmts if claims_known(store, s) for m in store.marks_written(s) if !claimed.contains(m.name)]
    let derived = flatten(
        [derived_unread(view.engine, view.file, store, s, claimed) for s in item.stmts if derived_alone(store, s)],
    )
    let own = [unread_at(a.span, a.name, "", claimed) for s in item.stmts if !declared_exported(view.engine, view.file, store, s) for a in marks_alone(view.engine, view.file, store, s) if !claimed.contains(a.name)]
    let gathered = flatten(
        [members_unread(view.engine, view.file, c!.name, c!.kind, c!.scope, claimed) for s in item.stmts for c in [store.collect_enum_parts(s)] if c != null && store.annotations_of(s).is_empty()],
    )
    written.concat(derived).concat(own).concat(gathered)
}

/// The bodies the generators the written item `at` of `file` wears made, typed: each method of an
/// impl an item a site of it made holds, read back where the file holds that item, past its written
/// ones.
fn spliced_bodies(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<StoredBody> {
    let sites = generator_sites(engine, file)
    let made = [site_generated(engine, file, s).items.length for s in sites]
    let first = item_count(engine, file)
    [StoredBody { store: read_item(engine, file, a.item).store, typed: b.typed } for i, s in sites if s.item == at for k in 0..made[i] for a in made_impls(engine, file, first + made.take(i).sum() + k) for b in typed_impl_bodies(engine, a)]
}

/// The impls the generated item `made_at` of `file` holds, each as a method's typing reaches it.
fn made_impls(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, made_at: int) -> List<ImplAt> {
    [ImplAt { file: file, item: made_at, params: impl_params(engine, m, d!), nth: nth } for nth, m in file_impls(engine, file)[made_at] for d in [impl_target(engine, file, m)] if d != null]
}

}

**Cause:** the items a derive generates sit after the file's own items, and no law on the layer ever typed their bodies, whether called or not. So an ill-typed, out-of-bound or misspelled rule spliced into a generated method was never refused.

  - "`int` does not implement `Sized`"
  - "no `fn lnog` is defined"
- **10ab1f8c:** which written item made each generated item is now worked out once per file. Per item, it had pushed cli CPU up 23%.
- **3e209abf:** generated items that contain none of the file's own code are skipped, since nothing in them could be reported there.

fn unclaimed(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    scope: FileScope,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    space: Space,
    name: string,
) -> Resolution {

    let prelude? = lent(engine, file, space, name) else { return Resolution.Unbound }
    Resolution.Named(prelude)
}

    }

/// Every name the top level of `file`, whose scope is `scope`, names a declaration by in `space`,

/// apart.
export fn seen_names(engine: QueryEngine, scope: FileScope, file: SourceFileAddress, space: Space) -> List<
    string,
> {
    let shared = module_bindings(engine, file.package_name, module_segments(file), true).shared
    let prelude = if file.package_name == PRELUDE { [] } else { module_names(engine, module_files(engine, PRELUDE, [], false)) }
    distinct(
        scope
            .own
            .names_in(space)
            .concat(shared.names_in(space))
            .concat(
                [d.name for d in prelude if lends(d, space) && scope.kept_apart(space, d.name).is_empty()],
            ),
    )
}

/// caller's known vocabulary syncs by class, anything else by text.
/// `END` syncs to the statement's end: past the next Break that stands
/// outside every brace the statement opened, or BEFORE a `}` it did not
/// open — a block it opened, on its line or after its failure, is its
/// own to close, so what stands around a statement that failed keeps
/// its shape. Stops at Eof.
fn sync_past<T, N>(cx: MatchContext<T, N>, target: string, entry: int, from: int) -> int {
    if is_end(target) { return sync_to_end<T, N>(cx, entry, from) }
    let known = cx.known_terminals.contains(target)
    let kind = cx.lex.kind_of(target)
    mut i = from
    while !cx.lex.is_eof(cx.tokens[i]) {
        let t = cx.tokens[i]
        let hit: bool = if known { cx.lex.wears_kind(t, kind) } else { cx.lex.lit_matches(t, target) }
        if hit { return i + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    i
}

fn token_lit<T>(lex: Lexeme<T>, lit_slots: Map<string, int>, t: T) -> int {
    let at? = lit_slots.get(lex.text(t)) else { return 0 - 1 }
    if lex.lit_matches(t, lex.text(t)) { at } else { 0 - 1 }
}

Name work has hit a decision point, and I've put it to the Lead.

**Done so far:** three cuts to literal text matches cut string compares on a cold cli check by 21.7%, already bundled for you.

**Why the rest needs a ruling:** the remaining name-shaped compares don't get cheaper by swapping in a Name at each site. Each lookup would have to intern its own name, which costs about what it saves:
- `found_at`, 7.7%: resolve's scope lookups over short parameter lists.
- `ItemView.holds`, 4.9%: the file-name check at each view hit.

The real payoff needs names interned upstream, so later compares are integer compares.

**The two options I gave the Lead:**
- **A. Grammar capture labels.** `binding_for` (3.0%) and `rebound` (1.4%) compare label strings on every capture. The labels are fixed per grammar, so they can be numbered once when the grammar is prepared. This stays inside std-grammar. I recommended starting here.
- **B. Identifiers interned from the syntax tape.** Lexer through to the AST, so every resolve, scope and `kept_apart` compare becomes an integer compare. This is broad and changes the AST and resolve types, so it would land in two stages.

I also have smaller literal cuts ready to take meanwhile: `continuing_op` (4.5%), `closer_of` (2.7%), the tape writer's kind lookup (2.4%) and `naming_of` (2.4%).

/// caller's own vocabulary of `.Named` class names.
export fn ready(g: Grammar, known_terminals: List<string>) -> Ready {
    mut ordinals: Map<string, int> = {}
    for j, r in g.rules { ordinals.set(r.name, j) }
    let prims = flatten([terminals_of(r.body) for r in g.rules])
    let terms = distinct([term for p in prims for term in some_list(p.class())])
    mut lit_slots: Map<string, int> = {}
    for j, text in distinct([text for p in prims for text in some_list(p.literal())]) { lit_slots.set(text, j) }
    Ready {
        g: listed_grammar(with_start_bits(with_branch_starts(slotted(g, terms, lit_slots)))),
        ordinals: ordinals,
        known_terminals: known_terminals,
        terms: terms,
        lit_slots: lit_slots,
        defects: g.defects(known_terminals),
        items: item_shape(g),
    }
}

impl Binding<T, N> {
    /// This binding, updated when its own label is `target`:
    /// accumulating `v` inside a repetition, replacing outright
    /// otherwise. Any other label passes through unchanged.
    fn rebound(target: string, v: Captured<T, N>, acc: bool) -> Binding<T, N> {
        if self.label != target { return self }
        self with { value: if acc { accumulate(self.value, v) } else { v } }
    }

    /// `rebound`'s whole-run twin: every value in `vs` folded in at
    /// once, for the label a repetition's own capture binds under.
    fn rebound_all(target: string, vs: List<Captured<T, N>>) -> Binding<T, N> {
        if self.label != target { return self }
        self with { value: accumulated_all(self.value, vs) }
    }
}

/// A new scope with `label` bound: accumulating inside repetitions,
/// last-wins otherwise.
fn bind_label<T, N>(bindings: List<Binding<T, N>>, label: string, v: Captured<T, N>, acc: bool) -> List<
    Binding<T, N>,
> {
    if !bindings.any(it.label == label) {
        let bound = Binding<T, N> {
            label: label,
            value: if acc { captured_many<T, N>([v]) } else { v },
        }
        return bindings.concat([bound])
    }
    [b.rebound(label, v, acc) for b in bindings]
}

file_path: /work/name-design.md
--- content ---
# B: identifiers as Names, interned upstream, ints downstream (ROADMAP #5)

## What carries a Name
- The type is std-program's `Name { id: int }` (names.av, 71df5b17). It is @sealed: only `name_of(text)`
  makes one. The id is dense and the PROCESS's own. `n.text()` answers the text.
- The source of every Name is the TAPE READ. The tape already numbers its texts once per tape
  (`NumberedTexts`; `TapeReader.text()` answers `texts[count()]`). The reader gains
  `name() -> Name`, which interns each distinct text slot of the tape ONCE: a lazily filled
  `List<Name?>` beside `texts`, indexed by the text's number. So an item read back pays one intern per
  distinct identifier, not one per mention. The writer gains `name(n: Name)`, which writes `n.text()`
  through the same `NumberedTexts`.
- The tape derive (core/copied_derive.av, the `untape_*`/tape writers it generates) learns one field
  kind, `Name`: read with `tape.name()`, written with `tape.name(n)`. The Matchable/kids derives need
  nothing (a Name carries no id of a node).
- Phase 1, the fields resolve compares: `Expr.Ident(name: Name)`, a pattern's bound name
  (`Pat.Bind`), `Param.name`, a lambda's params, a `let`'s binders. Resolve's frames, scope, overlays
  and lambda params become `List<Name>`, and lookups compare Names (one int each). The LOOKUP key
  arrives as a Name (from the Ident), so nothing is interned at the lookup.
- Phase 2, the declared names: `DeclaredName.name`, FileScope siblings, `Bound`. Map keys are strings
  only in this language, so a by-name table either stays keyed by `text()` or becomes a DenseWindow
  indexed by `id`, which is the process's own and never saved.

## How it is saved
- As TEXT, always: Name's `saved_bytes`/`written_into` write `NameText { text }`, and `read_from`/
  `from_saved_bytes` re-intern at load. The tape format does not change, since texts were always
  what it stored.
- Every hash, fingerprint, content key and print of a Name folds its TEXT (`folded_into`), never its
  id. A saved answer, a store key and a print are the same in every process.
- No id leaves the process: not in a saved answer, a diagnostic, a sort key, or a test's expected
  output.

## Bridge order (main's compiler builds each step)
1. Tape verbs only: `TapeReader.name()` with its per-tape intern slots, `TapeWriter.name(n)`, and the
   tape derive's `Name` field kind. No node uses it yet, so every tape is byte-identical.
2. `Expr.Ident(Name)` and its readers in one commit, about 47 match sites in 30 files: a site that
   needs text says `n.text()`, and one that compares compares Names. Resolve's scope and frames take
   `List<Name>`.
3. `Pat.Bind`, `Param`, lambda params and let binders the same way, one commit per node kind.
4. Phase 2 (declared names) as its own batch, after measuring 2–3.
None of this adds syntax or a compiler-checked law, so each step builds with the compiler before it.
The store's layouts change (a Name field is saved as a `NameText` record), so the first run of each
step re-derives cold, once. Each step's receipt: findings cmp-identical on cli, std-avrac and
std-program, gen-2; `check lawed` plus `WITNESS_ONLY=check`; census compares and retains; the
`--release` product cmp.

## What every lane touching Expr.Ident or resolve must know
- `.Ident(n)` binds a Name, not a string. Text is `n.text()`. Make one from source text with
  `name_of(text)`, never `Name { … }` (sealed).
- Compare Names with `==` (one int). Do not compare `n.text() == other.text()`: that is the string
  compare this exists to remove.
- An id is not a count and not an order. Sort by `text()` wherever order is visible (findings,
  diagnostics, listings). Two processes mint different ids for the same name.
- A Map cannot key on a Name (keys are strings). Key on `text()`, or index a DenseWindow by `id` for a
  table that lives only in this process.
- A Name in a saved type is saved as its text automatically (Name's own Saved verbs). Never hand-write
  its `id` into a record, key or hash.
- A template copied across files carries its Names as text and re-interns where it lands, so a
  splice never compares ids minted in another context.
- Merging across this batch: resolve conflicts in the type (string -> Name), then make every
  comparison in the conflicted body a Name comparison; a leftover `.text() ==` is the smell.

Option A and the four small literal cuts are done and bundled together with the earlier three cuts, five commits in all (base57..52436d3c). B's design is written up in `/work/name-design.md`, not built.

**The new work:**
- **40b976f3, capture labels as numbers (A):** the grammar executor numbers every label once when the grammar is prepared, so binding and reading a capture compares integers instead of label text.
- **52436d3c, four small cuts:** `continuing_op`, `closer_of`, the tape writer's node-kind lookup and the reserved-word check each now ask a set or map built once, instead of scanning.

**Results for all five commits** (cold second-generation build from a clean worktree):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| String compares, cold cli check | 301.4M → 201.7M (−33.1%; −21.7% after the first three) |
| Copies, retains, boxes | slightly down |
| Findings vs base57 | identical for std-program (85), std-avrac (2539), cli (1910) |
| CPU, cli, same-run pairs | 90.4/89.6 s vs 90.2/90.4 s, no measurable change |
| std-grammar suite | 56/56 |

A container restart killed the first measurement run after its builds finished. I resumed it from the census step, so all the numbers above come from complete runs.

**B, the design you asked for before building:**
- **The type:** names enter through the syntax tape. Each tape interns each distinct identifier text once, so the AST carries the existing sealed `Name`.
- **Saving:** always as text, re-interned when loaded. Every hash or fingerprint folds the text, and no id ever leaves the process.
- **Bridge order:**
  1. The tape gains a way to read and write a Name, with nothing using it yet.
  2. `Expr.Ident` and its roughly 47 match sites in 30 files, plus resolve's scope.
  3. The other binders, one node kind per commit.
  4. Declared names, as a separate batch.

  The current compiler builds each step.
- **What other lanes need to know:**
  - `.Ident(n)` binds a Name: use `n.text()` for its text, and compare Names with `==`, never by text.
  - Sort by text wherever order is visible.
  - A map can't be keyed by a Name, because map keys must be strings.

    mut writer = tape_writer()
    for value in values { writer.count(value) }

    writer.text(text)
    writer.finished()
}

fn declared(name: string) -> MetaType? {
    match name {
        "Label" -> label(),
        "Leaf" -> leaf(),
        "LeafId" -> leaf_id(),
        "Tree" -> tree(),
        _ -> null,
    }

/// A language that keeps `hidden` off its tapes.
fn tiny() -> Reading { Reading { declared: declared, role: role_of } }

fn role_of(f: Field) -> FieldRole { if f.name == "hidden" { .Carried } else { .Written } }

/// How a value of `kind` lies on a tape, spelled, or "none" when it has no shape.
fn lies(kind: Kind) -> string {
    let shape? = tiny().shape_of(kind) else { return "none" }
    lying(shape).spelled()
}

fn has_shape(kind: Kind) -> bool { tiny().shape_of(kind) != null }

@query
export fn file_rule_rows(engine: QueryEngine, program: string, file: SourceFileAddress) -> FileRuleRows {
    let src = rule_source(engine, file)
    let facts = flatten(
        [item_fact_findings(engine, program, file, at, src) for at in 0..item_count(engine, file)],

        )
    let found = [p.diag for p in walked(file_syntax_findings(engine, file, src), facts)]
    FileRuleRows { rows: rule_rows(src, found), said: [kept_diag(d) for d in found] }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Helpers of (engine, file, at, ...) that read refusals take the view instead; their thin law fns move to reads_view."""
import re, glob, os, sys

write = '--write' in sys.argv
src = {f: open(f).read() for f in glob.glob('*.av')}

HEAD = re.compile(r'\n((?:export )?fn (\w+)\(\s*engine: QueryEngine,\s*file: SourceFileAddress,\s*at: int,(.*?)\)( -> .*?)?\s*\{)', re.S)
def body_end(t, i):
    # the fn body runs to the first line that is exactly "}" after i, or the head line's own close
    line_end = t.index('\n', i)
    head_line = t[t.rindex('\n', 0, i) + 1:line_end]
    if head_line.rstrip().endswith('}') and head_line.count('{') == head_line.count('}'): return line_end
    return t.index('\n}', i) + 2
helpers = {}
for f, t in src.items():
    for m in HEAD.finditer(t):
        start = m.start(); end = body_end(t, m.end())
        body = t[m.end():end]
        if any(re.search(r'(?<![\w.])' + k + r'\(engine, file, at\)', body) for k in FAM):
            helpers[m.group(2)] = (f, start, end, m.group(3))
print(len(helpers), 'helpers:', ' '.join(sorted(helpers)))
# callers: every mention must be `H(engine, file, at, ` inside a one-line law reads fn `fn X(engine..., at: int) -> List<Found> { H(engine, file, at, ...) }`
THIN = re.compile(r'\n((?:export )?fn (\w+)\(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int\) -> (List<Found>|List<\s*Found,?\s*>) \{)')
ok = {}
for h in helpers:
    mentions = sum(len(re.findall(r'(?<![\w.])' + h + r'\b', t)) for t in src.values())
    calls = sum(len(re.findall(r'(?<![\w.])' + h + r'\(engine, file, at,', t)) for t in src.values())
    ok[h] = mentions == calls + 1
print('movable:', ' '.join(sorted(h for h in ok if ok[h])), '| kept:', ' '.join(sorted(h for h in ok if not ok[h])))
if not write: sys.exit(0)
reads = set(re.findall(r'\n    reads: (\w+)\n', ''.join(src.values())))
moved_laws = 0
for f in list(src):
    t = src[f]
    # helpers: head and body
    for h, (hf, _, _, _) in helpers.items():
        if hf != f or not ok[h]: continue
        m = re.search(r'\n((?:export )?fn ' + h + r'\(\s*engine: QueryEngine,\s*file: SourceFileAddress,\s*at: int,(.*?)\)( -> .*?)?\s*\{)', t, re.S)
        end = body_end(t, m.end()); body = t[m.end():end]
        for k, v in FAM.items(): body = re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])' + k + r'\(engine, file, at\)', v + '(view)', body)
        body = re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])(engine|file|at)\b(?!\s*:)', r'view.\1', body)
        head = 'fn ' if not m.group(1).startswith('export') else 'export fn '
        rest = m.group(2).strip().rstrip(',')
        newhead = f'{head}{h}(view: ItemView, {rest}){m.group(3) or ""} {{'
        t = t[:m.start()] + '\n' + newhead + body + t[end:]
    # thin law fns calling a movable helper

        name = m.group(2)
        if name not in reads: continue
        end = body_end(t, m.end()); body = t[m.end():end]
        hs = [h for h in helpers if ok[h] and re.search(r'(?<![\w.])' + h + r'\(engine, file, at,', body)]
        if not hs: continue
        stripped = body
        for h in hs: stripped = stripped.replace(h + '(engine, file, at,', h + '(view,')
        if re.search(r'(?<![\w.])(engine|file|at)\b(?!\s*:)', stripped): continue
        t = t[:m.start()] + '\n' + m.group(1).replace('(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int)', '(view: ItemView)') + stripped + t[end:]
        t = re.sub(r'(\n    )reads: ' + name + r'\n', r'\1reads_view: ' + name + '\n', t)
        moved_laws += 1
    src[f] = t
for f, t in src.items():
    if t != open(f).read(): open(f, 'w').write(t)
print(moved_laws, 'laws moved')
EOF

// THE THREE KINDS OF NAME A NODE CARRIES. Every name in the tree is
// text; what differs is WHAT IT KEYS, and that fact used to live only
// in the walks that read it. It is the payload's TYPE now, so the
// enum states it and a derive can read it. Free at runtime: each is

// `n.of` reads the text back.

/// A name that KEYS A SCOPE — a binder (`let x`, a parameter, a
/// pattern's bind, a fn's own name) or a READ of one (`x`, a call's
/// callee). The resolver walks the scope chain for it, so a
/// TEMPLATE filling one hands the node to the splice site's scope.
export type Scoped = string

/// A name that keys NO scope — a field, a method, a property, a
/// variant, a type parameter. It is answered by a shape the
/// compiler already knows, so filling one changes nothing about
/// where the node resolves.
export type Plain = string

Step 2 is bigger than the design assumed, so I've asked the Lead for a ruling before building it.

**The finding:**
- An identifier's name isn't a plain string. It's `Scoped`, defined as `type Scoped = string` in `core/nodes.av`.
- That one type is the name of every binder and every read: lets, consts, fn names, parameters, for-loops, pattern binds, and the type, trait, enum and component declarations. That's about 25 node types.
- Resolve compares an identifier against those binders, so an identifier can't become a Name while the binders stay strings. The compare would just turn back into a text compare.

**What I proposed:** make step 2 `type Scoped = Name` itself, which merges design steps 2 and 3. Declared names still come later.
- **Size:** making that one-line change and building gives 343 compiler errors across 37 files on the first pass. I'd expect around 500 sites once cascading errors surface.
- **Kind of work:** it's mechanical. Places that need text read it through `.text()`, the grammar builders create names with `name_of`, and comparisons stay `==`.
- **Tapes:** nothing new is needed, since step 1 already writes a Name as text.
- **Build order:** it still fits batch 60 on its own, and the current compiler can build it.

The scratch worktree is back to clean. I'll start the sweep once the Lead confirms Scoped-wide.

- **No text compares.** Comparing a name to a fixed word uses a verb that compares Names, not text. That keeps the closing sweep's count of `text() ==` at a true 0.

"""Applies the two mechanical rewrites to the refusals in an iteration's list; prints what it left."""

MINT = re.compile(r"argument 1 of `Scoped` wants `Name`, found `string`")
edits = collections.defaultdict(list)  # file -> [(line, col, kind)]
left = []
for p, e in rows:
    f, l, c = p.rsplit(':', 2)
    if MINT.search(e): edits[f].append((int(l), int(c), 'mint'))
    elif TEXT_WANTED.search(e): edits[f].append((int(l), int(c), 'text'))
    else: left.append((p, e))
done = 0; missed = []
for f, es in edits.items():
    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')
    for l, c, kind in sorted(set(es), key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1])):
        s = lines[l - 1]
        if kind == 'text':
            i = s.find('.of', c - 2)
            while i >= 0 and re.match(r'\.of\w', s[i:]): i = s.find('.of', i + 1)
            if i < 0:
                j = s.rfind('.of', 0, c + 40)

            if i < 0: missed.append((f, l, s.strip())); continue
            lines[l - 1] = s[:i] + 'scoped(' + s[i + 7:]

        else: t = 'use core.{scoped}\n' + t
    open(f, 'w').write(t)
print(done, 'rewritten;', len(missed), 'missed;', len(left), 'other')
for m in missed: print('  MISS', m[0].split('/src/')[-1], m[1], m[2][:120])
c = collections.Counter(re.sub(r'`[^`]*`', '`…`', e) for _, e in left)

fn place_key(cx: Checking, e: ExprId) -> string? {
    if cx.store.place_step(e) == null { return null }
    place_path(cx, e).join(".")

/// The names the place `e` is written down, in order.
fn place_path(cx: Checking, e: ExprId) -> List<string> {
    let step? = cx.store.place_step(e.text()) else { return [] }
    match step {
        .Root(name) -> [name.of],
        .Field(subject, name) -> place_path(cx, subject).concat([name.of]),
        .At(subject, _) -> place_path(cx, subject).concat(["[]"]),
        .Unwrap(subject) -> place_path(cx, subject).concat(["!"]),
    }
}

//! NUMBERS KEPT BY SMALL KEYS THAT SIT CLOSE TOGETHER, as the ids of one item's nodes do: an array
//! offset by the lowest key met, so a lookup is one bounds check and one load, nothing is hashed,
//! and the array is as wide as the keys are spread. It grows to either side by doubling, so a key
//! met out of order costs amortized constant time. An identity: every holder sees one window.
use @std.meta.{identity}

/// What a window holds. Values are never negative.
@identity
export type DenseWindow = {
    /// The key slot zero stands for.
    lowest: Cell<int>,
    /// Each slot holds one more than its key's value, or zero when it holds none.
    slots: Cell<List<int>>,
}

export fn dense_window() -> DenseWindow {
    let slots: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
    DenseWindow { lowest: Cell.new(0), slots: slots }
}

impl DenseWindow {
    /// The value under `key`, absent when there's none.
    fn get(key: int) -> int? {
        let at = key - self.lowest.get()
        let slots = self.slots.get()
        if at < 0 || at >= slots.length { return null }
        let held = slots[at]
        if held == 0 { return null }
        held - 1
    }

    fn put(key: int, value: int) {
        self.reach(key)
        self.slots.set_at(key - self.lowest.get(), value + 1)
    }

resolve: a scope keys a binder by its name and its origin, two ints

Resolve's scopes keyed every binder by a string built from its name and the file that wrote it
(`name@origin`), compared text against text in the fn's seats and the lambda frames, and hashed it
into a map for each open overlay. A key is now a `ScopeKey { name, origin }`, compared as two ints.

The open bindings are one stack, the program scope's first and then each open overlay's in order,
with the place each open overlay starts. A bind pushes onto it, a lookup reads it latest first (so a
later binding shadows the earlier, as Map.set did), and closing an overlay pops its bindings off.
A capture set still names its captures by the key's text, read only when a frame captures.

/// A declared enum's variant table, in declaration order — the
/// index IS the runtime tag, and a payload (when the variant
/// carries one) rides slot 1 of the value.
@derive(Fingerprint)
export type EnumSig = { names: List<string>, payloads: List<List<TypeId>> }

/// Names listed for help text — one wording everywhere.
fn named_list(names: List<string>) -> string {
    joined(["`${n}`" for n in names], ", ")
}

impl StructSig {
    /// A named field's slot, when declared — THE lookup every
    /// consumer shares.
    fn slot_of(name: string) -> int? {
        found_at(self.names, name)
    }

    /// The fields, listed for help text.
    fn listed() -> string {
        named_list(self.names)
    }

    /// Whether slot `j` is a `state` field — its slot holds a `Cell`
    /// while its reads answer what the cell holds.
    fn state_at(j: int) -> bool {
        if j < self.states.length { self.states[j] } else { false }
    }

    /// Whether the field named `name` is a `state` field.
    fn state_named(name: string) -> bool {
        let j? = self.slot_of(name) else { return false }
        self.state_at(j)
    }

    /// Why the record leaves `name` out, when it does so on purpose.
    fn lacked(name: string) -> string? {
        let l? = self.lacking.find(it.field == name) else { return null }
        l.why
    }
}

impl EnumSig {
    /// A named variant's TAG, when declared.
    fn tag_of(name: string) -> int? {
        found_at(self.names, name)
    }

    /// What the variant CARRIES, in order — empty for a unit variant.
    fn payloads_of(name: string) -> List<TypeId> {

# gdb -x callers.py: tallies the callers of the functions named in CALLERS_OF (comma list of symbols),
# two frames up, never stopping; writes the tally to CALLERS_OUT at exit.
import gdb, os, re, collections
tally = collections.Counter()
nm = lambda s: re.sub(r'\$([0-9A-F]{2})', lambda x: chr(int(x.group(1), 16)), s or '?')
class Count(gdb.Breakpoint):
    def stop(self):
        f = gdb.newest_frame().older()
        a = nm(f.name()) if f else '?'
        g = f.older() if f else None
        b = nm(g.name()) if g else '?'
        tally[(self.location, a, b)] += 1
        return False
def done(ev):
    with open(os.environ['CALLERS_OUT'], 'w') as o:
        for (l, a, b), v in tally.most_common():
            o.write(f"{v} {nm(l)} <- {a} <- {b}\n")
gdb.events.exited.connect(done)
gdb.execute('set pagination off'); gdb.execute('set confirm off')
for s in os.environ['CALLERS_OF'].split(','):
    Count(s, internal=False)
gdb.execute('run')

/// A hash's bits spread so its low ones pick a slot.
fn spread(h: int) -> int {
    let x = (h ^ shifted_right(h, 32)).wrapping_mul(0 - 4658895280553007687)
    x ^ shifted_right(x, 29)

/// The first free slot from where `h` lands.
fn free_slot(slots: List<int>, h: int) -> int {
    mut slot = spread(h) & slots.length - 1
    while slots[slot] != 0 { slot = slot + 1 & slots.length - 1 }
    slot
}

/// `count` slots holding every id so far.
fn slots_holding(hashes: List<int>, count: int) -> List<int> {
    mut slots = [0 for _slot in 0..count]
    for id, h in hashes { slots[free_slot(slots, h)] = id + 1 }
    slots
}

    hash_word(hash_word(hash_word(h, n), avra_str_word_at(text, 0)), avra_str_word_at(text, n - 8))

//! THE FOLD — a tag and its parts as one number, shared by every
//! fingerprint space in the compiler. It stands in its own file
//! because `@derive(Fingerprint)` CALLS it: a derive's file is typed
//! while the annotated file is still registering, so the fold living

use @std.relation.stable.{Scope}

/// A variant tag folded with its parts, in order — THE fingerprint
/// fold, for nodes and for every query value's hash alike.
export fn fp(tag: int, parts: List<int>) -> int {
    mut h = fp_mix(tag, parts.length)
    for p in parts { h = fp_mix(h, p) }
    h
}

/// A SEQUENCE FOLDS TO ONE VALUE, so a payload's ARITY is fixed and
/// the boundary between two of them cannot move. Spliced flat,
/// `f<A>(B)` and `f<A, B?>()` wore one fingerprint — a pinned type
/// and an argument are the same value in a flat list. SHARED across
/// every fold space, so tag 105 is claimed wherever it is called.
export fn fp_list(parts: List<int>) -> int { fp(105, parts) }

/// In-process rolling hash; both operands normalized under a prime so
/// mixing never overflows, negative payloads included. The crypto
/// tier arrives with the on-disk cache.
fn fp_mix(h: int, v: int) -> int {
    mut nv = v % 1000000007
    if nv < 0 { nv = nv + 1000000007 }
    (h * 131 + nv + 7) % 1000000007
}

}

```
cat > /work/bin/testfix.py <<'PY'
# testfix.py <errors.list>: wraps string literals a Scoped seat refuses in `scoped(...)`, rewrites
# `Scoped("w")` to `scoped("w")` and `X == "w"` on a Scoped to `X.spells("w")`, and adds `scoped` to
# each touched file's `@std.avrac.core` import. Prints what it could not place.
import sys, re, collections
rows = [l.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.strip()]
by_file = collections.defaultdict(list)
for loc, err in rows:
    path, line, col = loc.rsplit(':', 2)
    by_file[path].append((int(line), int(col), err))
lit = re.compile(r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"')
for path, errs in by_file.items():
    src = open(path).read().split('\n')
    touched = False
    # right to left within a line, so earlier columns stay put
    for line, col, err in sorted(errs, key=lambda e: (e[0], -e[1])):
        s = src[line - 1]
        i = col - 1
        m = lit.match(s, i)
        if 'wants `Name`, found `string`' in err and m and s[:i].endswith('Scoped('):
            src[line - 1] = s[:i - 7] + 'scoped(' + s[i:]
            touched = True
        elif ('carries `Scoped`, found `string`' in err or 'is `Scoped`, this is `string`' in err) and m:
            src[line - 1] = s[:i] + 'scoped(' + m.group(0) + ')' + s[m.end():]
            touched = True
        elif 'compares matching types, found `Scoped` and `string`' in err and m and re.search(r'\s*==\s*$', s[:i]):
            pre = re.sub(r'\s*==\s*$', '', s[:i])
            src[line - 1] = pre + '.spells(' + m.group(0) + ')' + s[m.end():]
            touched = True
        else:
            print(f'UNPLACED {path}:{line}:{col} {err}')
    if touched:
        text = '\n'.join(src)
        if not re.search(r'\bscoped\b', text.split('\nfn ')[0].split('given')[0]) or 'scoped,' not in text and 'scoped}' not in text and ', scoped' not in text:
            m2 = re.search(r'use @std\.avrac\.core\.\{', text)
            if m2:
                text = text[:m2.end()] + 'scoped, ' + text[m2.end():]
            else:
                first_use = re.search(r'^use ', text, re.M)
                text = text[:first_use.start()] + 'use @std.avrac.core.{scoped}\n' + text[first_use.start():]
        open(path, 'w').write(text)
PY

def counts_of(text):
    """The census lines of one run -> {counter: n}."""

        if m:

    return got


def edited(text, kind, old, new):
    """`text` with one edit made: `old`, which stands in it once, becomes `new`; a `rename` renames the
    word `old` wherever it stands. Raises where the edit does not stand as written."""
    new = new.replace("\\n", "\n")
    if kind == "rename":
        word = re.compile(r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(old))
        if not word.search(text):
            raise ValueError("no `%s` to rename" % old)
        return word.sub(new, text)
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError("`%s` stands %d times, not once" % (old, text.count(old)))
    return text.replace(old, new, 1)

/// One `let` definition of the program, in order.
export type Def = { name: Scoped, stmt: StmtId }

/// A binder's KEY in the scope tables: its name, and the file that wrote a template's text, or
/// `OWN_WRITING` for the file's own. A template's `tmp` and a hole's `tmp` are two keys, which is the
/// whole of hygiene. Two keys compare as two ints.
export type ScopeKey = { name: Scoped, origin: int }

/// The origin a key of the file's own writing wears.
export const OWN_WRITING: int = 0 - 1

/// Where a key is bound inside the open overlays: the overlay, and the binding.
export type OverlayHit = { overlay: int, binding: Binding }

/// A binder an arm opens, with the file that WROTE its text — a
/// generated pattern's name and its arm's value may come from
/// different runs, and the binder wears its own.
export type Bound = { name: string, origin: FileId? }

# rowdiff.py <tagA> <tagB> [callee-regex]: per calling function, rowcalls to runtime fns matching the
# regex (default: list reads), A -> B, the largest rises first.
import sys, re, subprocess, collections
pat = re.compile(sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else r'avra_(array_get|slot_get|array_get_owned|list_get)')
nm = lambda s: re.sub(r'\$([0-9A-F]{2})', lambda x: chr(int(x.group(1), 16)), s)
def load(t):
    rows = [l.split() for l in open(f'/work/out/sites-{t}.raw') if l.startswith('rowcall: site')]
    rows = [r for r in rows if pat.search(r[5])]
    names = subprocess.run(['addr2line', '-f', '-e', f'/work/out/avra.census-{t}'], input='\n'.join(r[2] for r in rows), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')[0::2]
    c = collections.Counter()
    for r, n in zip(rows, names): c[(nm(n).split('$')[0][3:], r[5])] += int(r[3])
    return c
a, b = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
print('total', sum(a.values()), '->', sum(b.values()))
d = sorted(((b[k] - a[k], k) for k in set(a) | set(b)), reverse=True)
for v, k in d[:22]: print(f'{v:+12} {a[k]:>11} -> {b[k]:>11} {k[0][:90]} {k[1]}')
print('...')
for v, k in d[-8:]: print(f'{v:+12} {a[k]:>11} -> {b[k]:>11} {k[0][:90]} {k[1]}')
PY

//! VALUES INTERNED AS DENSE IDS. Inside one process a value's identity is a small int, minted the
//! first time an equal value arrives: equality is one compare, and a memo over the value is a dense
//! list indexed by it. Finding a value's id costs one cheap hash and one exact comparison, so asking
//! for it is cheaper than most answers it keys. An id means nothing outside the table that minted it,
//! so `InternId` has no `Saved` impl and can never cross; a boundary carries the value's CONTENT KEY.

//! A content key is folded by the value's own type over two LANES (`HIGH_LANE`, `LOW_LANE`), each a

# gdb -x callers2.py: tallies the call chains (CALLERS_DEPTH frames up) into the functions named in
# CALLERS_OF (comma list), never stopping; writes the tally to CALLERS_OUT at exit.
import gdb, os, re, collections
depth = int(os.environ.get('CALLERS_DEPTH', '6'))
tally = collections.Counter()
nm = lambda s: re.sub(r'\$([0-9A-F]{2})', lambda x: chr(int(x.group(1), 16)), s or '?')
short = lambda s: re.sub(r'^av_@std/(avrac|program)/src/', '', nm(s)).split('$')[0]
class Count(gdb.Breakpoint):
    def stop(self):
        f = gdb.newest_frame().older(); chain = []
        while f is not None and len(chain) < depth:
            chain.append(short(f.name())); f = f.older()
        tally[tuple(chain)] += 1
        return False
def done(ev):
    with open(os.environ['CALLERS_OUT'], 'w') as o:
        for chain, v in tally.most_common(): o.write(f"{v} " + ' <- '.join(chain) + "\n")
gdb.events.exited.connect(done)
gdb.execute('set pagination off'); gdb.execute('set confirm off')
for s in os.environ['CALLERS_OF'].split(','): Count(s, internal=False)
gdb.execute('run')
PY

/// A mark folded into a node's print: its code, and what it carries as one value.
export type Stamp = { code: int, value: int }

fn no_prints() -> Stamped {
    Stamped {
        identities: list_cell(),
        stamps: list_cell(),
        prints: list_cell(),
        settled_in: list_cell(),
        pass: Cell.new(0),
        passes: Cell.new(0),
        settled: Cell.new(0),
        stale: Cell.new(false),
    }
}

fn no_stamps() -> List<Stamp>? { null }

impl Stamped {
    /// A node added, printed as what it is.
    fn added(identity: int) {
        self.identities.push(identity)
        self.stamps.push(no_stamps())
        self.prints.push(identity)
        self.settled_in.push(0)
    }

    /// Node `at` wears the mark `code`, carrying `value`.
    fn stamp(at: int, code: int, value: int) {
        let kept = [s for s in self.stamps.get()[at] ?? [] if s.code != code]
        let stamps = [s for s in kept if s.code < code]
            .concat([Stamp { code: code, value: value }])
            .concat([s for s in kept if s.code > code])
        self.stamps.set_at(at, stamps)
        self.refold(at)
        self.written(at)
    }

    /// Node `at` was written: outside a settle, one a settle derived makes every print stale.
    fn written(at: int) { if self.pass.get() == 0 && at < self.settled.get() { self.stale.set(true) } }

### 2026-11-20T23:46:54 AGENT
Census list reads count only `array_get` and `slot_get` (and their owned forms); `.length` and character reads aren't counted. So a print costs 2 counted reads, not 3. The 9.76M prints are about 19.5M of the excess, not 29M. That changes the arithmetic, so I'm reporting the measurement before building, as asked:

<to_controller>Lead: who calls the name-identity fold (cold cli check, gdb, 9.76M calls; each call is 2 counted list reads, since census counts get/slot reads and not `.length`, so about 19.5M of the 35M excess, not 29M):
1. `Ident.identity`, 4.62M: at allocation (`alloc_expr`) 2.34M, and again at settling (`resettled_expr`) 2.27M. A settle re-derives every node's identity, including leaves whose payload never changed.
2. The matcher's shallow folds (`text_print_of`), 1.71M: `rule_pass.node_candidates` 0.82M, `match_typed_node` 0.38M, `shallow_at` 0.30M.
3. Params inside `FnDecl.identity` (`Param.identity`), 1.26M: at allocation and at settling, plus 0.15M in shallow.
4. `Call.identity`, 0.89M (allocation 0.45M, settling 0.44M); `FnDecl` 0.48M; `Let` 0.36M; the rest under 0.13M each.

So identity is already folded once per node allocation. The waste is the settle re-folding nodes whose own payload didn't change. Plan (c), exact, with estimated savings:
- An `Ident` leaf keeps its identity at settle unless replaced since the last settle. The arena already tracks that: `rewritten_from` is the lowest replaced index, forgotten at each settle. About −4.5M.
- The same rule for the name parts of `Call`, `FnDecl` params and `Let`, by caching each node's own-leaves fold beside its identity. About −3M.
- The shallow fold reuses that cached own-leaves fold. About −3.4M.
- Outside (c): a tape reading takes its number eagerly, as a plain field (−3.3M); the intern table's Cell-held `hashed`/`same` (2 reads × 2.8M probes) about −5.6M, if `@identity` allows plain fn fields.

Total about −19.8M against the 28.7M needed. On these estimates (c) narrows the gap but doesn't close it. It's still a net improvement on its own. I'll build the `Ident` settle cut first and slice it; that turns the estimate into a measurement before more is built.</to_controller>

### 2026-11-21T04:10:38 RUN Bash [SmHwR64S]
```
cd /work/out && cat > /work/bin/families.py <<'PY'
import sys, re, subprocess, collections
pat = re.compile(r'avra_(array_get|array_get_owned|slot_get|slot_get_owned)$')
nm = lambda s: re.sub(r'\$([0-9A-F]{2})', lambda x: chr(int(x.group(1), 16)), s)
def load(t):
    rows = [l.split() for l in open(f'/work/out/sites-{t}.raw') if l.startswith('rowcall: site')]
    rows = [r for r in rows if pat.search(r[5])]
    names = subprocess.run(['addr2line','-f','-e',f'/work/out/avra.census-{t.split("-")[0]}'], input='\n'.join(r[2] for r in rows), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')[0::2]
    c = collections.Counter()
    for r, n in zip(rows, names): c[nm(n).split('$')[0][3:]] += int(r[3])
    return c
F = [('intern table probes (name_of)', r'interned\.av\.Interned\.(standing|id_of|minted)|free_slot'),
     ('name text reads', r'Name\.text$|Interned\.value_of'),
     ('name prints (identity, shallow)', r'Name\.text_print|text_print_of'),
     ('tape name reads', r'TapeReader\.(name|text)|slot_held|tape_name'),
     ('settle: identity kept / refolded', r'resettled_expr|kept_since_settle|rewritten_from|Stamped\.refold|Expr\.identity|Stmt\.identity'),
     ('scope by name (kept_apart, by_text)', r'item_scope\.av'),
     ('statement names (let_name/let_named)', r'let_name'),
     ('nodes read (arena)', r'Arena\.node_at|SyntaxArena\.expr$|SyntaxArena\.stmt$'),
     ('saved tables (ReadTable, HashKeyedTable)', r'hash_keyed_table')]
for w in sys.argv[1:]:
    a, b = load(f'F3-{w}'), load(f'SQ-{w}')
    fam = collections.Counter(); seen=set()
    for k in set(a)|set(b):
        for name, rx in F:
            if re.search(rx, k): fam[name] += b[k]-a[k]; seen.add(k); break
    other = sum(b[k]-a[k] for k in set(a)|set(b) if k not in seen)
    print(f'=== {w}: total {sum(b.values())-sum(a.values()):+,}')
    for name, _ in F: print(f'{fam[name]:>+14,}  {name}')
    print(f'{other:>+14,}  everything else')
PY
